newsitem.title: India: India rupee up vs forward dlr on low interest hopes.
newsitem.headline: India rupee up vs forward dlr on low interest hopes.

text.p: The Indian rupee traded stronger against the forward dollar on Monday afternoon on low interest rate expectations following the central bank's credit policy announcement last Tuesday, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) released its credit and monetary policy on April 15, announcing steps to bring about a fall in interest rates.
Some banks announced cuts in their prime lending rates last week, following the credit policy announcement.
Dealers said they also expected a drop in long-term rates.

"Basically, it (falling forward premia) is a continuation of the trend after the credit policy," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Combined with the current strength of the rupee, this has led to forward dollar sales by both exporters as well as in the interbank market."
Dealers said forward dollar premia were being pushed down by a combination of factors...a strong rupee, good domestic liquidity and expectations of low interest rates in the future.
The Indian rupee has been on the upswing in recent times and was quoted at 35.762/772 per dollar in latest deals against the day's opening 35.79/80.
In the forward market October-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 83/86 paise against opening quotes of 85/88 and the weekend close of 94/97.
